promptAsSent:
Use the image_gen tool to generate exactly one image, then stop. Do not write files, run commands or edit anything.

Attached reference images, in order:
Image 1: Geometry/layout authority
Image 2: Identity: the intact stones, their material, colour, light and rendering

Use case: sketch-to-render. RESKIN image 1, the authoritative geometry guide, into the DAMAGED state of seven overhead field-stone sprites for a top-down tactical game: the same stones after heavy fire has cracked and chipped them. Image 2 is the intact sheet and is the IDENTITY authority: the same stones, the same painterly stone, the same soft upper-left light and the same rounded forms. Image 1 says where the damage goes.
Preserve image 1 exactly: 2:1 canvas, 4 columns x 2 rows, the eighth frame (bottom right) EMPTY. Every stone keeps the outline the guide gives it; the bites out of its rim are fresh chips. Do not add, merge, move or enlarge stones.
Camera STRAIGHT DOWN from directly above, orthographic plan view, as in image 2.
Damage: the dark lines in the guide are deep cracks running across each stone; chipped edges show fresh stone; a little ash-grey dust on the stone tops. The stones are still whole and still rounded. Keep image 2's bleached bone-grey heat-fused stone, its dull grey-olive glass glaze and its scorch-darkened rims; the glaze is crazed and flaked off along the cracks; fresh breaks show the same muted ash-grey stone, never white. Stay as light as image 2, no lighter. NOT faceted, NOT low-poly. They must read clearly at about 50 pixels across: clear masses, a few bold cracks, no fine noise.
No grass, soil, scorch disc, ground patch or cast shadow outside the stones, no labels, no text, no border. True transparent background around and between every stone. Keep the 2:1 canvas.
